researcher_notes:
COMPANY CONFIRMED REAL. Rocla AGV Solutions, HQ Jarvenpaa, Finland (FI). Part of the Mitsubishi Logisnext group since 2009 (verbatim from Rocla NA brochure p3: 'Since 2009, part of Mitsubishi Logisnext group'). IMPORTANT ENTITY NOTE: the legal entity Rocla Oy was RENAMED 'Logisnext Europe Oy' in May 2026 (rocla-agv.com/about-us/company-presentation/); several 2026 product pages already read 'Logisnext Europe offers...'. 'Rocla' continues as the AGV brand and rocla-agv.com is the live product site. ~500 employees in Jarvenpaa; Mitsubishi Logisnext group ~11,000 staff / 17 countries. Company roots 1942; AGV business since 1983; >1,000 AGV systems and >7,000 vehicles delivered.

PORTFOLIO SHAPE: Rocla builds ONLY forklift-type AGVs (automated versions of warehouse trucks). There are NO tugger/tow-tractor AGVs and NO autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) in the lineup — all vehicles are fixed-infrastructure guided AGVs (laser triangulation off reflectors), not free-navigating AMRs. Do not create Tugger AGV or Mobile AMR records for this supplier.

CURRENT LINEUP = 9 models, taken from the live product index rocla-agv.com/agv-solution/automated-guided-vehicles/ : ACT, ART, and seven AWT (Automated Warehouse Truck) variants (Very Narrow Aisle, Counterbalance, Straddle, Conveyor, Reel Fork, Roll Clamp, Bale Clamp). AWT is a modular platform: common tractor unit + mast + application-specific load handler.

DISCONTINUED / EXCLUDED: the ATX / ATX12 pallet mover (1250 kg, 1800 mm lift) appears in the 2019/2020 Rocla brochures but is NOT on the current product index — treated as discontinued and deliberately NOT entered. Also excluded: 'Rocla High Density Warehouse' / mobile racking (rack-integrated system, not a vehicle) and FleetController (software only).

PLATFORM-LEVEL FACTS (apply to all 9 vehicles; sources: rocla-agv.com FAQ + Rocla NA brochure pp.36-37 'Navigation and Energy', p.7 'Safety and Environment'):
- Navigation: laser triangulation off wall-mounted reflectors = 'the most common navigation method in Rocla AGV systems'. Also offered: magnetic-spot navigation (magnets set into the floor) and wire navigation (buried inductive wire); combinations are supported.
- AP0 VOCAB GAP: Rocla's 'Spot Navigation' = discrete magnetic spots/pucks in the floor, which is NOT the same as continuous 'Magnetic Tape'. I did NOT map it to Magnetic Tape. Recommend an AP0 'Magnetic Spot' option (same gap class as the previously flagged QR-code nav gap).
- infrastructure_free = false for every model (reflectors, floor magnets or floor wire are always required).
- Batteries: open lead-acid (most common), maintenance-free lead-acid, quick-charge lead-acid, and Li-Ion (FAQ: Li-Ion rechargeable in as little as ~1 h). Runtime quoted only as a vague fleet-wide '8-14 hours depending on vehicle type, environment and load weight' — too vague and too cross-model to enter as battery_runtime; left NULL.
- Charging: manual charging, opportunity charging (= automatic charging), manual battery exchange, automatic battery exchange station (BES). => autonomous_charging = true, battery_swap_capable = true, platform-wide.
- Safety: every current product page states the model 'meets/is designed to meet the ISO 3691-4 safety standard requirement'. Minimum safety devices on all Rocla AGVs: front laser scanner, rear bumpers or laser scanners, safety PLC, e-stops in all corners, safety edge around the vehicle, warning lights + audible signals. CE marked, Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC.
- Fleet software: FleetController (proprietary). Interfaces per brochure p.35: WMS, ERP/MES, OPC server (I/O), TCP/IP socket, FTP, direct DB connection.
- OPC CAVEAT: the brochure says 'OPC-server', which in a 2020 document most likely means OPC Classic/DA, not OPC-UA. I did NOT set integration_capability=OPC-UA anywhere. Left as WMS/ERP/MES only.
- VDA 5050: NOT mentioned anywhere on rocla-agv.com or in any brochure. vda5050_compatible deliberately left NULL for all models — NOT set to false either, since absence of a claim is not a denial.
- NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE for any Rocla model (all left NULL): max_speed, vehicle_length/width, operating_temp min/max, humidity, IP rating, gradient, stop/drop/pick accuracies, turning radius, max_fleet_size, functional_safety_level, charge_time, battery_runtime.

UNIT CONVENTION: Rocla's EU site publishes lift height and aisle width in METRES and payload in kg. All values below converted to mm/kg. The North American brochure publishes imperial — used only for cross-checking, never as the primary value.

CROSS-CHECK RESULT (EU 2026 site vs Rocla NA brochure 08/2020): ART and VNA AWT match to within rounding across both sources (see per-product notes) — HIGH confidence. Counterbalance, Straddle, Roll Clamp and Bale Clamp payloads have INCREASED vs the 2020 brochure (newer generation); I used the current EU site values and flagged the delta in notes.

products.notes: Official page verbatim: 'in aisles that have as little as 3 m free space, can handle loads as heavy as 1600 kg and have a lifting capacity of up to 10 m' plus 'Thanks to the new frame model, the new ARTsmf can operate in 2.85 m free-space aisles without compromising the lifting capacity'. min_aisle_width=2850 uses the ARTsmf frame (best case, correct for KO_IF_GT semantics); the baseline frame needs 3000 mm. CAVEAT: Rocla states aisle as FREE-SPACE aisle width — confirm the tender uses the same definition. CROSS-CONFIRMED by Rocla NA brochure 08/2020 p22: 3,527 lbs = 1600 kg, 393 in = 9,982 mm (~10 m), 118 in = 2,997 mm (~3 m) — three independent matches. Won Red Dot Design Award 2025 and was nominated for materialfluss Produkt des Jahres 2025. manual_usage NOT set: the page's 'compatibility with existing warehouses operated by manual reach trucks' means coexistence with manual trucks in the same aisle, NOT that the vehicle itself has a manual driving mode — that would be an over-read.

Official page verbatim: 'ACT can lift heavy loads up to 6 m in as narrow as 2.6 m aisles' and 'Available as forkover and counterbalance'. mast_type=Triplex from the Rocla ACT launch article and the ACT news page ('a triplex mast reaching up to 6 metres'). onboard_ui=true: page describes a highly responsive touchscreen on the vehicle with colour-coded information plus LED fins acting as turn signals.

*** max_payload DELIBERATELY OMITTED — UNRESOLVED CONFLICT ***
Two sources disagree and neither is a primary EU spec sheet: (a) Logisnext Americas ACT page states 2,400 lb = ~1,088 kg; (b) a secondary/aggregated source quotes '1.6 t, and 800 kg to 6 m'. The Rocla EU product page itself states NO payload figure at all. Because max_payload is a KO_IF_LT field, entering either value risks wrongly qualifying or disqualifying Rocla. Leave NULL and obtain the ACT datasheet from Rocla directly.
Also note the (b) figure implies a DERATED capacity at height (1.6 t at low lift vs 800 kg at 6 m) — if that structure is confirmed, the KO-relevant value at full 6 m lift is the lower one, which matters a lot for tender matching.

drive_type OMITTED on purpose: ACT ships as BOTH forkover (straddle) and counterbalance, so a single drive_type value would be wrong for half the configurations. Consider two variant records once the datasheet is available.
Awards: iF Design Award 2024, Red Dot Design Award 2024, Automation Product Innovation of the Year (Archies) 2024.

products.product_name: Rocla Very Narrow Aisle AWT (VNA AWT)
products.notes:
Official page verbatim: 'it can operate in aisles as narrow as 1.6 m, handle loads up to 1200 kg, and has a lifting capacity of up to 12.75 m'. Also: 'equipped with telescopic load handling forks or a turret head for trilateral turning (-90 deg...0 deg...+90 deg) of load forks'. 1600 mm aisle sits exactly at the bottom of the normal VNA band (1600-2000 mm) — plausibility OK.
CROSS-CONFIRMED by Rocla NA brochure 08/2020 p27 ('AWT Narrow Aisle'): 2,645 lbs = 1,200 kg (exact match), 68 in = 1,727 mm aisle, 472 in = 11,989 mm lift. Payload matches exactly; the current generation has grown the lift (11.99 m -> 12.75 m) and tightened the aisle (1.73 m -> 1.60 m). Used the current EU values.
drive_type='VNA Turret': the turret head is the OPTION and telescopic forks are STANDARD, so a pure man-down telescopic VNA truck is the base build. 'VNA Turret' is the closest AP0 value and the turret is genuinely offered — but flag this if drive_type is ever used as a KO.
navigation/guidance: the 2020 brochure lists 'Dual navigation' for the VNA series, and the Bring Logistics (Skedsmo, NO) reference — 9 Rocla VNA AGVs — states verbatim 'laser navigation in the master aisle and inductive wire navigation in the narrow aisles'. Hence Laser Reflector + Inductive Loop and guidance=Wire. This is the standard VNA arrangement (rail guidance is the alternative but is not documented for Rocla).
Two dimensional drawings are offered on the page for sub-variants 'AWTcs' and 'AWTct', both for ISO 1200x800 pallets — the drawings sit behind a lead-capture form so vehicle_length/width could not be read.
The Bring reference also documents real throughput: 173 pallets/hour across 9 vehicles into 81,200 pallet places at 419 in (~10.6 m) racking height — a FLEET figure, so deliberately NOT entered as a per-vehicle throughput field.

Official page verbatim: 'given its lifting height of up to 8,4 m and permitted loads of up to 2,500 kg, it facilitates both two- and four-pallet transport'. Also 'Compatibility with drive-in racking', 'For push-back racks', 'For gravity racks/free flow racks', 'Ideal solution for applications where support legs cannot be used' — the last point is what makes it counterbalanced rather than straddle.
multi_load_compatibility=true is DERIVED from the explicit 'two- and four-pallet transport' claim (carries multiple loads simultaneously), not guessed.
CONFLICT WITH OLDER SOURCE: the 2020 NA brochure quotes the AWT Counterbalance at 4,409 lbs = 2,000 kg and 275 in = 6,985 mm. The current EU page says 2,500 kg / 8,400 mm. Treated as a newer generation; used the current site. Do not merge the two.
station_applications 'Gravity rack' from the explicit gravity/free-flow rack claim; 'Floor' from block/floor storage use.

Official page verbatim: 'Lifting height of up to 8.6 m', 'Loads of up to 2,500 kg', and 'capable of load-on-load operation and deep-stacking pallets with stable loads. Its high lifting capacity and support structure are well-suited for both conveyor handling and high lifting.' The support structure = straddle/support legs, hence drive_type=Straddle Stacker.
Described by Rocla as 'the most common AWT ... works well in different applications and has an appealing price/performance balance' — this is the volume model of the AWT platform.
LIFT CROSS-CONFIRMED: 2020 NA brochure p16 gives 338 in = 8,585 mm, matching the current 8.6 m almost exactly.
PAYLOAD CONFLICT (flagged, not resolved): the same 2020 brochure page says 'Loads up to 11,023 lbs' = 5,000 kg, which is 2x the current site's 2,500 kg. Note that 11,023 lbs also appears for the AWT Conveyor, where the current site clarifies it as '2 x 2,500 kg' — so the 5,000 kg is most likely a TWO-PALLET total for a twin-load build rather than a single-load rating. I used the current site's single-load 2,500 kg because max_payload is a KO_IF_LT field and the conservative, explicitly-current value is the safe one. If a tender needs >2,500 kg on this model, verify with Rocla before disqualifying.

*** PRODUCT-TYPE CAVEAT — READ BEFORE IMPORT ***
This is a CONVEYOR AGV: an AWT chassis carrying a powered roller-conveyor deck, not a fork truck. It is neither a tugger nor an AMR, so 'Forklift AGV' is the least-wrong of the three permitted product_type values, but it is not a clean fit. I therefore left lifting_height NULL and set stacking_capability=false so it cannot wrongly satisfy a rack-stacking or lift-height KO.

max_payload=5000: official page states 'Loads of up to 2 x 2,500 kg' — entered as the 5,000 kg TOTAL vehicle capacity. If the tender's payload requirement is per-load rather than per-vehicle, the applicable figure is 2,500 kg. CROSS-CONFIRMED by the 2020 NA brochure p19 ('AWT Conveyor ... Loads up to 11,023 lbs' = 5,000 kg) and p33 ('Loads up to 2 x 5,511 lbs' = 2 x 2,500 kg) — the two brochure entries agree with the current site.
multi_load_compatibility=true: carries two loads simultaneously, explicitly.
Transfer height is stated as 'up to 950 mm' with 'variable transfer height as an option' and 'vertical conveyor functionality' as an option. There is NO AP0 field for conveyor transfer height — 950 mm was deliberately NOT written into lifting_height, because it is a handover height to a fixed conveyor, not a racking lift height. Recording it there would be a real KO-matching hazard.
Official page: 'The Conveyor AWT meets the ISO 3691-4 safety standard requirement. It has comprehensive safety features like 360 deg safety fields and side clearance monitoring.'
industries_served listed verbatim on the page.

Official page verbatim: 'The forks can be either fixed or adjustable, and can handle loads of up to 8,000 kg', 'Designed specifically for reel handling', 'Ideal system for horizontal reel transport', 'available as a solution for light, medium, and heavy loads'. 8,000 kg is at the heavy-duty end but well within the plausible band for a paper-mill reel handler — no plausibility concern.
lifting_height DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the current page states no lift height. The 2020 NA brochure's 'AWT Reel' gives 283 in (~7,188 mm), but that same brochure also gives a payload of 13,227 lbs = 6,000 kg vs the current 8,000 kg, so it is a different generation and I will not transplant its lift height onto the current model. Leave NULL.
stacking_capability OMITTED for the same reason — cannot be confirmed without a lift height.
load_type OMITTED: this vehicle handles paper/tissue/plastic REELS, not pallets. 'Custom Carrier' would be a guess about how the tender vocabulary treats reels; better left NULL than mis-set on a categorical matching field.
fork_spread NOT set: 'fixed or adjustable' does not say whether adjustment is powered/automatic or a manual setup operation. Both AP0 values ('Manual'/'Auto') would be speculation.
industries_served listed verbatim on the page.

Official page verbatim: 'Lifting height of up to 7.25 m', 'Loads as great as 6,000 kg', 'The clamps can handle loads up to 6,000 kg, and the modular design enables combining tried-and-tested components with automation.' Rotating clamps are documented for this family in the 2020 brochure ('AWT Clamp ... Rotating clamps').
LIFT CROSS-CONFIRMED: 2020 NA brochure 'AWT Clamp' = 283 in = 7,188 mm, matching the current 7.25 m. Payload has been uprated (7,716 lbs = 3,500 kg in 2020 -> 6,000 kg now); used the current site value.
A dimensional drawing labelled 'AWTcc ISO diameter 1530 - 3500 kg' is offered on the page but sits behind a lead-capture form, so it could not be read; note it implies a 3,500 kg sub-variant exists alongside the 6,000 kg top build.
load_type OMITTED: handles paper/film ROLLS, not pallets — see the Reel Fork note.
stacking_capability=true is derived from the 7.25 m lift into roll storage (well above a transport-only vehicle), consistent with the brochure's 'operation of reel storages'.

Official page verbatim: 'It offers a lifting height of up to 7.25 m and a load capacity of up to 6,000 kg', plus the application description 'transfers from a bale-wrapping line or a truck being unloaded to pulp storage. It can also operate pulp storage, transport material to de-wiring stations, and prepare truck loading.'
Mechanically the same AWT clamp platform as the Roll Clamp AWT (identical 7.25 m / 6,000 kg headline figures) with a bale clamp instead of a roll clamp.
CONFLICT WITH OLDER SOURCE: the 2020 NA brochure's 'AWT Pulp Clamp' quotes 3,306 lbs = 1,500 kg at 283 in — a much smaller machine. The current 6,000 kg is a newer/heavier build; used the current site value and did not merge.
load_type OMITTED: handles pulp BALES, not pallets.
station_applications 'Dock' derived from the explicit 'truck being unloaded' / 'prepare truck loading' statements. trailer_loading/trailer_unloading NOT set to true: loading a truck from the dock face is not the same capability as driving INTO a trailer, and Rocla does not claim in-trailer operation.
